title: Positive solver tolerance gives only a tolerance-stamped compile guarantee
statement: At a finite D partition stable at gain tolerance epsilon, every admissible individual relocation has gain at most epsilon, including each admissible disagreement with the deterministic terminal nearest-centroid rule, priced against the original partition. Compilation additionally requires every positive-weight prediction disagreement to be admissible. Positive tolerance alone does not imply distinct centroids or admissibility: singleton ties can force refusal. No bound on simultaneous reassignment, global optimality gap or population loss follows. The implementation evaluates exact-formula gains numerically in its retained score subspace; this is not an interval-arithmetic certificate.
assumptions: positive gain tolerance; positive-weight atoms with duplicate labels consistently merged
positive-definite retained information in the working score coordinates; exactly K nonempty cells
stability against all individual relocations preserving positive source-cell weight
successful compilation requires all positive-weight prediction disagreements to preserve source-cell weight
deterministic lowest-index argmin; zero-weight rows carry no information or label-reproduction guarantee

proof_location.section: D6. Exact finite inductive closure / compiler

role: what a real solver can actually claim
